cues: The rule no will after if applies to conditions, and there are four recognised exceptions, so don't over correct.
Willingness: if you will wait here, I'll call the manager.
Insistence: if you will eat so much sugar, expect toothache.
A remote chance, with should: if you should meet him, give him my regards.
And when if means whether, after wonder or ask, it is not a condition at all: I wonder if he will come.
